summary: gRPC long-poll disconnects behind corporate TLS-inspecting forward proxy on private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent gRPC stream disconnects (server-initiated RST / RESET) for long-polling requests from private deployment when traffic routes through their corporate TLS-inspecting forward proxy.

Impact: Production streaming endpoints drop ~3-10% of user sessions during business hours; affects inference continuity for chat features. Customer sees elevated error rates and has paused canary rollout.

Environment: Private deployment in customer VPC (FinLite) peered to Redwood control plane. Egress via corporate forward proxy (explicit HTTP CONNECT) performing TLS interception and ALPN rewriting. Client SDK uses HTTP/2 over TLS to connect to Redwood ingress (grpc).

Steps to reproduce:
1) From customer app hosts behind corporate proxy, establish streaming gRPC call to Redwood endpoint with keepalive enabled (interval 20s).
2) Let stream remain idle >90s, then send prompt.
3) Observe server-side reset and client gRPC error UNAVAILABLE / HTTP/2 GOAWAY in logs.

Observed behaviour: Streams terminate with HTTP/2 GOAWAY or RST_STREAM; connection resets coincide with proxy idle timer and rewritten ALPN tokens. TCP remain open but HTTP/2 layer fails to negotiate. No client TLS certificate issues.

Expected behaviour: Long-lived gRPC streams should survive through proxy with transparent CONNECT and keepalive preserved; graceful keepalive probes should be proxied and not trigger shutdown.

Relevant logs/observations:
- Customer tcpdump: repeated TLS renegotiation attempts and ALPN advertised as "http/1.1" after proxy re-write.
- Redwood ingress (nginx sidecar) logs: proto negotiation mismatch: expected h2, got h1 upgrades; recorded GOAWAY with code NO_ERROR immediately prior to user-facing error.
- Packet capture shows proxy injecting TLS payload inspection frames and altering ALPN list.
- No model pull errors; only streaming termination.

Attachments: customer-provided pcap (s3 link), proxy config snippet, ingress logs excerpt.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: corporate proxy is rewriting TLS ClientHello ALPN during re-key/idle timeout, causing mismatch when ingress expects h2. Alternative hypothesis: keepalive probes are converted to HTTP/1.1 pings by proxy, causing nginx to signal GOAWAY.

Actions taken:
- Reproduced failure in staging with a simulated forward proxy that rewrites ALPN -> reproduced GOAWAY within 2 minutes.
- Verified Redwood ingress accepts HTTP/2 and honours ALPN; when ALPN changed mid-connection, HTTP/2 is torn down.
- Captured tcpdump on customer-host and ingress; confirmed proxy inserts TLS rewrap and advertises only http/1.1 in rekey handshake.
- Tested forcing HTTP/1.1 fallback: client switched to HTTP/1.1 and resumed unary calls (non-streaming), but streaming unavailable.

Temporary mitigation identified: configure SDK to enable HTTP/1.1 fallback for non-streaming paths, and/or set proxy to preserve ALPN/h2 in TLS rewrap. Longer-term: document proxy configuration requirements and add health-checkable header to detect ALPN rewriting and auto-failover.

Open questions:
- Can we detect ALPN rewrite at connection start and present actionable error to customer?
- Should we implement a graceful downgrade path that proxies streaming over websocket when h2 unavailable?

Next steps assigned to SRE and SDK teams.

[2026-03-13 11:03] SRE (Miguel Santos): Reproduced in staging with mitmproxy configured to strip h2 ALPN. Confirmed GOAWAY from ingress. Adding ingress-side logging to show ALPN on accept.
[2026-03-13 14:45] Customer (FinOps Lead - Emily Chen): We've pushed a proxy change earlier this week; can revert to previous image to test. Will try overnight and report.
[2026-03-14 07:31] Support (Aisha Nguyen): Customer reverted proxy config; observed connection stabilised in limited test. Requesting formal workaround and guidance for permanent fix.
[2026-03-14 10:05] SDK (Lara Kim): Adding feature request to SDK to surface explicit ALPN mismatch warning and automatic websocket streaming fallback. Filed PR referenced above.
resolution:
Workaround: Customer reverted proxy TLS rewrap policy to preserve ALPN and increased proxy idle timeout to 15 minutes. This reduced streaming disconnects to <0.1% during monitoring window.

Permanent fix / follow-up:
- SRE to publish runbook on ALPN preservation for corporate forward proxies (confluence link included).
- SDK team to prototype websocket fallback for streaming clients where ALPN/h2 unavailable.
- Add detection logic in ingress to log ALPN mismatch and return a clear error (400 with guidance) instead of silent GOAWAY.

Status: Mitigation applied by customer; monitoring continues for 72 hours. Owner for follow-up: Aisha Nguyen (Support) / Miguel Santos (SRE) / Lara Kim (SDK).
